Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Subramonium Prasad
 Or
% 12.09.2024
1.

The Petitioners have approached this Court for quashing FIR No.622/2019 dated 13.11.2019 registered at Police Station Mehrauli for offences under Section 498A, 406 & 34 IPC on the ground that the parties have entered into a settlement.

2. The facts of the case reveal that FIR No. 1388/2016 dated 05.07.2016 registered at Police Station Mehrauli for offences under Section 376/506 IPC was also lodged by Respondent No.2 against the Petitioner No.1.

After one month, i.e., on 16.08.2016, Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No.2 got married at the Arya Samaj Tigri Marriage Mandal, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi and the parties have lived together for a period of about six years now.
3. Material on record discloses that disputes arose between the parties and FIR No.622/2019 dated 13.11.2019 was registered at Police Station Mehrauli for offences under Section 498A, 406 & 34 IPC was lodged against the Petitioners.
The parties decided to part ways and a divorce This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2024 at 04:25:29 petition under Section 13(B) (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed by both sides for dissolving the marriage on mutual consent which was allowed on 03.02.2023 and a sum of Rs.6 lakhs has been given for the said purpose.
4. It is stated that the settlement is an oral settlement.

Before granting divorce, the Trial Court has recorded that the parties have entered into a settlement and a sum of Rs.6 lakhs has been given by Pankaj Sharma Ors vs The State Anr on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62205346/
1 the Petitioner No.1 to Respondent No.2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, there is no mention that Respondent No.2 has agreed not to proceed with the criminal case.

5. Even though there is no mention of the same, in view of the facts of this case, this Court is inclined to issue notice to Respondent No.2 to verify as to whether Respondent No.2 has agreed not to proceed with the complaint under Section 498A IPC and as to whether this was also the part of the settlement which was entered into between the parties when the divorce was granted.
6. Issue notice.
7. Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
8. On taking steps, let notice be issued to Respondent No.2 through all permissible modes, including Dasti.
SUBRAMONIUM PRASAD, J SEPTEMBER 12, 2024 hsk
